title: How Long Does Vinyl Plank Installation Take? Room-by-Room Timeline
meta: Vinyl plank installation takes about a day per 500 sq ft on a flat subfloor. Wills Flooring gives a room-by-room timeline for Snohomish homes, plus delays.
keywords: how long does vinyl plank installation take, LVP installation time per square foot, vinyl plank flooring install timeline, how long to install vinyl plank whole house, vinyl plank stairs installation time, Snohomish vinyl plank installation

blocks.lead: A two-person crew installs about 500 to 700 sq ft of click-lock vinyl plank per day on a flat, ready subfloor, so a bedroom is half a day, a main floor is one to two days, and a whole Snohomish house is three to five.
blocks.detail: Tear-out, subfloor prep and stairs are what stretch the schedule. Wills Flooring installs vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft in labor plus $100 per stair, and the calendar below is what those numbers buy.

blocks.html: People ask this for a practical reason: they want to know how many days the dog goes to the neighbor's, whether the kitchen is usable Thursday night, and whether a Snohomish farmhouse on acreage with a crawlspace and three generations of flooring is a two-day job or a two-week one. The honest answer has two parts. Laying the plank itself is fast. Everything that has to happen before the first plank goes down is where the time hides.

blocks.note: Times are for a two-person crew laying click-lock or rigid-core plank. Glue-down plank adds roughly half a day per 500 sq ft for adhesive open time.

blocks.text: The five things that add days

items.title: Tear-out
items.text: Carpet and pad come up fast, about an hour per room including staples and tack strip. Glued sheet vinyl and ceramic tile do not. Tile over a 1990s Clearview kitchen can take a full day to remove and haul, and it leaves thinset that has to be ground flat before plank goes down.

items.title: Subfloor flattening
items.text: Vinyl plank needs a subfloor flat to about 3/16 in over 10 ft. Old Snohomish farmhouses and homes on Fobes Hill with crawlspaces often have joist crowns and sagging spots. Sanding high spots and troweling floor patch into low ones is a half day to a full day, plus overnight for patch to cure.

items.title: Moisture and crawlspace issues
items.text: A damp crawlspace or a wet slab in a daylight basement shows up on the meter before it shows up under the floor. If readings are high we stop, tell you, and the fix belongs to a crawlspace or drainage contractor, not to a floor schedule.

items.title: Acclimation and delivery
items.text: Rigid-core plank needs about 48 hours in the house at living temperature before installation, longer if it sat in a cold garage or the house is heated by a wood stove that swings the temperature. This is calendar time, not crew time, but it still moves the finish date.

items.title: Stairs
items.text: Each stair is a tread, a riser and a nosing cut and fitted by hand, roughly 40 minutes to an hour per step. A 13-stair run is a day on its own, priced at $100 per stair. Open-sided stairs and winders sit at the top of that range.

items.title: Furniture and appliances
items.text: A room we walk into empty takes the time in the table. A room with a bed, dresser and a wall of bookshelves adds an hour on each end. Refrigerators, ranges and washers add time to disconnect and reconnect, and we tell you in advance which ones we will handle.

blocks.text: A typical whole-house job in Snohomish, day by day

items.text: Plank is delivered and stacked flat in the rooms it will go in. The house stays at normal living temperature. You clear closets and small items; we handle the heavy pieces on the day.
Carpet, pad, tack strip and any old vinyl come out of the main floor. Subfloor is checked for flatness and moisture, squeaks are screwed down, high spots sanded, low spots patched.

Underlayment if the product needs it, then plank from the longest straight wall out. Doorways get undercut jambs so plank slides under trim instead of being cut around it. By evening the kitchen and living room are walkable.
items.note: 1,000 sq ft × $2.50 = $2,500 in labor for this floor.

items.text: Stairs are built tread by tread with matching nosings. The upstairs hallway ties in at the top landing.
Bedrooms go quickly since they are rectangles. Transitions at bathrooms and closets, shoe molding or baseboard back on, appliances reconnected, and a walkthrough with you before we load the truck.

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn two days into a week

items.html: Ordering the plank the week of the job. Backorders and short boxes are the number one cause of a stalled install. Order with 7 to 10 percent extra and have it on site two days early.
Assuming the old floor is flat. A quick check with a straightedge at the estimate saves a surprise day of leveling. We do it on every Snohomish estimate because so many homes here sit on crawlspaces.
Skipping acclimation because the product is waterproof. Waterproof is not the same as temperature-stable. Cold plank installed tight expands in a warm house and lifts.

Leaving the plumbing to chance. If a toilet or a washer has to come out, know who is doing it. We handle appliance moves as a quoted line; a corroded shutoff valve is a plumber's job and a lost half day.

blocks.title: For homes with dogs and mud, which in Snohomish is most of them:
blocks.text: Plan the entry and mudroom for the last hour of the last day so the crew is not tracking gravel across new plank, and keep the dogs out for the first night while the transitions set. The floor itself is walkable immediately.
How to get a firm day count

items: Measure the rooms and count the stairs, doorways and transitions. Doorways matter more than square footage.
Tell us what is under the current floor. Carpet, glued vinyl, tile and hardwood each set a different tear-out day.
Say whether the house is heated by a furnace, heat pump or wood stove. It changes acclimation.
Decide what you are moving and what we are moving.
Book the free estimate. We check flatness and moisture on the spot and write both the price and the day count into the quote.

faq.q: How long does it take to install 1,000 sq ft of vinyl plank?
faq.a: About two days for a two-person crew on a flat, ready subfloor, plus a day of tear-out if the old floor is carpet or glued vinyl. At Wills Flooring the labor is 1,000 × $2.50 = $2,500. Tile removal, leveling or a staircase in the same job each add roughly a day.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank be installed in one day?
faq.a: A single room or a small main floor up to about 600 sq ft can be torn out and installed in one long day if the subfloor is flat and the plank has already acclimated in the house for 48 hours. Anything with stairs, tile removal or leveling will run into a second day.

faq.q: How long does vinyl plank need to acclimate before installation?
faq.a: About 48 hours in the rooms where it will be installed, at normal living temperature. Snohomish homes heated by a wood stove or left cool during the week need the full two days or more so the plank reaches the temperature it will live at before it is locked in tight.

faq.q: How long after installation can I walk on vinyl plank?
faq.a: Immediately for click-lock and rigid-core floating floors. Furniture can go back the same day; use felt pads. Glue-down vinyl plank should have light traffic only for 24 hours and no heavy furniture or rolling loads for 48 to 72 hours while the adhesive cures.

faq.q: How long does it take to put vinyl plank on stairs?
faq.a: Roughly 40 minutes to an hour per stair, so a straight 13-step staircase is a full day. Each tread, riser and nosing is cut and fitted individually. Wills Flooring prices stairs at $100 per stair. Open-sided treads and pie-shaped winders take longer than closed straight steps.

faq.q: Does old floor removal add much time?
faq.a: Carpet and pad add about an hour per room. Glued sheet vinyl adds half a day. Ceramic tile is the slow one, often a full day for a kitchen including grinding the thinset flat afterward. We quote tear-out as its own line at the free estimate so the day count is honest.
